text: Welcome to Oracle Financial Reporting, the fifth course in the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path. You've already configured the General Ledger, Payables, Receivables, and the rest. Now it's time to get the numbers out of the system. We start with the landscape: why Oracle Fusion has so many different reporting tools.

Different readers want different things from the same transactions. A board member wants a clean, consistent Income Statement. A collections analyst wants to slice open receivables right now, without waiting on IT. A compliance team wants a pixel-perfect scheduled report that goes out the same way every period. A controller wants live ledger balances in Excel they can pivot five different ways. No single tool is great at all four jobs.

So Oracle Fusion gives you four purpose-built tools instead. Financial Reporting Studio builds formatted statements like the Income Statement and Balance Sheet. OTBI handles ad hoc, real-time exploration and dashboards. BI Publisher produces pixel-perfect, often scheduled output like regulatory forms. And Smart View brings Excel-native analysis plus collaborative reporting packages.

All four live inside Oracle Fusion itself, not a separate application. The Financial Reporting Center sits inside General Accounting. OTBI shows up in a shared catalog and embedded right inside work areas like Payables. BI Publisher reports run from Scheduled Processes. And Smart View is a Microsoft Office add-in that connects straight out to your Fusion environment.

Keep this map in your head as we go chapter by chapter: one chapter per tool, then a final chapter on the specific financial and operational reports a working consultant produces every month. Up next, lesson two: the Reports and Analytics pane, the catalog that ties a lot of this together.
